about: The RemoteFM1 releases the web installer offers, newest first: the first is the latest ("latest": true), the one index.html and the engine install; the others are history (a unit running one is offered the latest). sha256 is the package's (firmware/remote-X.Y.fwsc), as firmware/SHA256SUMS lists it: test_installer.mjs checks the two agree, and the page checks it again in the browser before any write. A release built from another tree than repo's names it in source.

notes: weavejam's build of RemoteFM1 (branch velocity, commit 08bae22, built by its fwsc CI): Note On velocity 1..127 from the keys' carbon pills (CTL-1's sensing, fm1-base / felucca-bsp, MPL-2.0); the top row too.
Poly aftertouch for held keys F3..C5: lean into a key after it has settled (not in its first 250 ms, when the pill is still compressing).
A note-on waits up to ~15 ms for its velocity; a key with no reading plays at 100 as before. Hosts that don't know the new capability bits work as with 0.1.
Tested on an FM-1 on 2026-10-25: velocities 1..127 with no fallbacks, chords and releases clean, MASTER, LEDs, buttons and encoders as 0.1.1. The update loader and safeguards are 0.1.1's.
The FM-1 as a USB panel: its keys, buttons, knobs and MASTER go to the computer as MIDI; the computer draws its screen and lights its LEDs.
Makes no sound by itself: a firmware running on the computer (this site's player, FM1VST, fm1remote) plays.

New in 0.1.1: a firmware whose image is larger than the app area (Baud Girl's can be) is refused before anything is written, by the FM-1 and by its update loader; 0.1 could have committed it truncated. Install such a firmware through the official V15.
The update loader is TransitFM1 0.1.3's, byte for byte (answers ota-FM-1_900). The panel and the protocol are 0.1's, the build tested on an FM-1 on 2026-10-18.
TransitFM1's safeguards: ChoralRoot's boot stub, its own update loader (the next firmware's first sector written last), the boot guard; answers every installer as the official V15.
